messages:
Sophia L: Quick design thread — we need a working pattern for per-customer telemetry isolation (traces/logs/metrics). Goals: tenant-level RBAC for Console, independent retention policies, and clean cost allocation.
Kevin B: Are we leaning toward physical separation (per-tenant indices / buckets) or logical namespaces (prefixes + query scoping)?
Maria C: Physical separation = strongest isolation but blows up index/bucket count and complicates infra. Logical namespaces + backend-enforced scoping is operationally simpler.
Devon R: My +1 is to do routing in the collector: extract tenant_id from header/attribute, add a `tenant` resource attribute, then route to exporters that tag the index/bucket prefix. Example (sketch):
```
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}

processors:
  attributes:
    actions:
      - key: tenant_id
        action: insert
        from_context: http.request.header.x-tenant-id
  batch: {}

exporters:
  elasticsearch/tenantA:
    endpoint: https://es.local
    index: traces-tenantA-%{+YYYY.MM.dd}
  elasticsearch/default:
    endpoint: https://es.local
    index: traces-default-%{+YYYY.MM.dd}

service:
  pipelines:
    traces/tenantA:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [attributes, batch]
      exporters: [elasticsearch/tenantA]
    traces/default:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [attributes, batch]
      exporters: [elasticsearch/default]
```
Sophia L: Nice. Two followups: 1) metrics cardinality — embedding tenant_id on every metric label will explode series. 2) retention enforcement — prefer ILM/policy per-tenant or object storage cold tier?
Anna P: +1 on the metrics concern. For metrics we should hash tenant into a shard label (e.g., `tenant_shard`) for aggregation/alerts, and only keep full tenant_id on traces/logs where it's needed for per-customer debugging.
Kevin B: RBAC note: Console must never trust client-side filtering. Backend APIs must automatically scope queries to the tenant context (enforced by token), and dashboards should be multi-tenant-aware by default.
Maria C: For retention I'd propose: hot indices per-tenant for X days (configurable), then move to cold S3-backed storage with a tenant prefix (e.g., s3://rdi-telemetry/{tenant}/traces/...). That gives us per-tenant retention without huge ES index count in long term.
Devon R: Implementation caveat: routing to separate exporters per tenant is fine for a few dozen tenants, but we need a fallback router for dynamic tenants. We can use a single exporter that takes `index` or `bucket` interpolation from attribute. Collector supports attribute-based index formatting in some exporters. Fallback to default index if tenant missing.
Anna P: We should also think about query isolation at the search-layer: avoid exposing tenant prefixes in search APIs; instead map tenant token -> internal namespace id. Prevent devs from constructing arbitrary index names in queries.\notel-bot: deploy-bot: collector: v0.55.2 deployed to staging (otel-collector-staging), config reload at 2025-06-04T15:12:01Z :white_check_mark:
Kevin B: Cost allocation: tag every ingest with tenant metadata so downstream billing job can compute tokens/ingest bytes. Need sampling rules too — e.g., default 10% for debug traces unless customer opts in.
Maria C: Action items I propose: 1) Prototype collector pipeline that sets resource.tenant and writes traces to tenant-prefixed S3 + short-lived ES indices. 2) Prototype metrics path with hashed tenant_shard label. 3) UI API for tenant retention/RBAC config. I'll own the prototype and demo.
Devon R: I can draft the collector config and exporter interpolation helper this week. Will add tests for fallback routing.
Sophia L: SGTM. I'll open an RFC in rfc/telemetry with the example config and retention UX mockups. Maria — please link prototype in the RFC when ready.
Kevin B: Thanks — please @channel when RFC is up so infra team can review potential operational costs.
